title: Nasi Lemak in KL: Where to Eat It and What to Order
metaDescription: Nasi lemak in KL by area: Kampung Baru, Pavilion and Imbi, Central Market and late branches in TTDI. What is on the plate and how to get there from KLIA2.

contentBlocks.content: Nasi lemak in KL is breakfast, lunch and supper. You can eat it at a Kampung Baru stall, a food court inside Pavilion, a kopitiam near Central Market or a branch open past midnight. This guide explains what comes on the plate, what to add, and where to find it in each part of Kuala Lumpur you are likely to stay in. Each place links to its Google Maps listing, so you can plan the walk from your hotel before you land.
Key Takeaways
What is nasi lemak? Rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaves, served with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, hard boiled egg and cucumber (Tourism Malaysia).
How much does a plate cost? Tourism Malaysia puts it between RM2 and RM20, depending on where you buy it (Tourism Malaysia).
Where do I start? Kampung Baru for Malay stalls, Pavilion and Imbi if you stay in Bukit Bintang, and Central Market or Medan Pasar if you stay near Chinatown.
Is it halal? It depends on the shop. Some KL nasi lemak is served with pork. Look for the JAKIM halal certificate at the counter before you order.
How do I get there from KLIA2? Book the bus to KL Sentral. It leaves from the Transportation Hub on Level 1 (ttklia.com).
What is nasi lemak, and what do you order?

Nasi lemak means rice cooked in coconut milk. Tourism Malaysia describes the rice as cooked with pandan leaves and served with sambal, a spicy chilli paste, plus anchovies, peanuts, hard boiled egg and cucumber slices (Tourism Malaysia). Its Kuala Lumpur guide adds that the rice can be spiced with ginger, star anise and cinnamon, and that rendang, a thick meat curry, often comes on the side (Tourism Malaysia).

That plain plate is the base. Most shops let you add a side. At Nasi Lemak Burung Hantu the menu highlights are rendang daging (beef rendang), ayam berempah (spiced fried chicken) and udang petai (prawns with stink beans) (NLBH). At Chinese kopitiam outlets you may see fried pork belly instead. Point at what you want, and ask for the sambal on the side if you are unsure about the heat.
Order the plain plate first. Add one side once you have tasted the sambal.
Kampung Baru: Jalan Raja Muda Musa and Jalan Daud

In Kampung Baru, several nasi lemak shops sit within a few streets of each other. Nasi Lemak Wanjo is at 8 Jalan Raja Muda Musa. Google Maps lists it as a Malay restaurant serving traditional rice plates cafeteria style in a long standing space. Its online ordering page offers self pickup at the counter and delivery within 30km, with a RM20 minimum for delivery (Nasi Lemak Wanjo).

On the same road, Nasi Lemak Pak Aji is at 4 Jalan Raja Muda Musa. Google Maps describes it as an open air eatery known for its sambal and nasi lemak. On Jalan Daud, Nasi Lemak Kukus Ayam Kampung at 18f is listed as a coffee shop. Kukus means steamed, so the rice here is steamed rather than boiled.

All three are listed on Google Maps as Malay restaurants or coffee shops. That is not halal certification, so look for the JAKIM certificate at the counter. Walk Jalan Raja Muda Musa first, then pick the shop that suits you.
Bukit Bintang, Pavilion and Imbi

Staying in Bukit Bintang? You have nasi lemak inside the malls. Pavilion Kuala Lumpur on Jalan Bukit Bintang has two. Nasi Lemak Shop @ Pavilion Kuala Lumpur is on Level 1, Lots 1.52.00 and 1.53.00. Together Nasi Lemak is in Food Place, Lot 1.29.04 on Level 1, open daily from 10am to 9.30pm (Together Nasi Lemak).

Together Nasi Lemak describes its food as Chinese kopitiam style, with fragrant rice and spiced coconut fried pork belly (Together Nasi Lemak). It serves pork, so it is not for halal diners. Its Imbi outlet is in the Ho Wah Shun coffee shop at 33 Jalan Kamuning, near TRX, open daily from 10am to 8pm (Together Nasi Lemak).

On Jalan Galloway, 100 Years House is listed on Google Maps as a coffee shop at number 10. The kopitiam there, Uncle Sam Kopi, lists a nasi lemak series on its menu, seats you across four floors with a rooftop, and opens daily from 8.30am to 10pm (Uncle Sam Kopi).
For the rest of the area, from Jalan Alor to Lot 10, read the Bukit Bintang food guide. If you stay here, the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC is the one to book.
Chinatown, Central Market and Masjid India
Inside Central Market, The Nasi Lemak Gerai is at unit FS02. Gerai is Malay for stall. Combine it with a walk through the market.

On Medan Pasar, Hock Kee Heritage is on the ground floor of 13 and 15. Hock Kee calls itself a Nanyang kopitiam and names fragrant nasi lemak among its classics (Hock Kee). Ask about pork before you order.
North of Medan Pasar, Nasi Lemak Burung Hantu Semua House is at GF-07 on the ground floor of Semua House, Jalan Bunus 6. The brand lists this branch as open from 8am to 10pm (NLBH).
Arriving late? The first night in KL guide matches dinner to each airport bus stop. Check the JAKIM certificate at each counter if you eat halal.
Further out: late nasi lemak in TTDI and Old Klang Road

Burung hantu is Malay for owl. Nasi Lemak Burung Hantu says it took the name because it keeps its doors open late into the night (NLBH). Its TTDI branch is in the Teeko directory, listed under supper, with coconut rice served with fried chicken or telur (egg), at 14 Lorong Rahim Kajai 14.
The brand lists two TTDI outlets. The one on Lorong Rahim Kajai 13 opens from 11am to 1am, and the one on Lorong Rahim Kajai 14 from 5pm to 2am. Its Desa Sri Hartamas branch lists 24 hours (NLBH).
On Old Klang Road, Together Nasi Lemak at K88 Food Court on Jalan Kangkong, Taman Goodwood, opens daily from 4pm to 1am (Together Nasi Lemak). It serves pork.
These are a taxi or e-hailing ride from the city centre. For more late food, see the supper in Kuala Lumpur guide.
Getting into KL from KLIA2

Buses to the city leave from the KLIA2 Transportation Hub on Level 1. Follow the Bus signs after the arrival hall (ttklia.com). From KL Sentral, continue to your hotel by train or taxi. The fare is shown on the booking page and includes the terminal fee. Staying in Bukit Bintang? Book the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC instead.

contentBlocks.content: Frequently Asked Questions
What is in nasi lemak?
Nasi lemak is rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaves, served with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, hard boiled egg and cucumber (Tourism Malaysia). Fried chicken and rendang are common add-ons.
Where can I eat nasi lemak near Bukit Bintang?

Pavilion Kuala Lumpur has Nasi Lemak Shop and Together Nasi Lemak on Level 1. Together Nasi Lemak also has an outlet on Jalan Kamuning in Imbi, and Uncle Sam Kopi on Jalan Galloway lists nasi lemak on its menu.
Is nasi lemak in KL halal?
Not all of it. Some kopitiam versions come with pork. A Google Maps label such as Malay restaurant is not certification, so look for the JAKIM halal certificate at the counter.
Can I eat nasi lemak late at night in KL?
Yes. Nasi Lemak Burung Hantu lists its Desa Sri Hartamas branch as open 24 hours and its second TTDI branch until 2am (NLBH).
Which nasi lemak in KL should I pick?
Search for best nasi lemak kl and you get rankings built on reviews. This guide does not rank. It tells you where each shop is and what it serves, so you can choose by where you are staying.
How much is nasi lemak in KL?
Tourism Malaysia puts a plate between RM2 and RM20, depending on where you buy it (Tourism Malaysia). Sides cost extra.
Conclusion

Nasi lemak in KL is easy to find wherever you stay. Go to Kampung Baru for Malay stalls, Pavilion and Imbi near Bukit Bintang, Central Market and Medan Pasar near Chinatown, and TTDI when it is late. Opening hours change, so open each Google Maps link to check them before you go. Then book your bus from KLIA2 to KL Sentral on ttklia.com and eat your first plate tonight.
